sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Fifa president Gianni Infantino indicated greater funding could go to members from reserves. In a letter to continental confederations, he supported additional funding following pressure over his withdrawn proposal to sell stakes in tournaments.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Uefa and Concacaf demanded Fifa pays $10m to all 211 members from its reserves. Infantino faced a backlash over the aborted plan and calls for his resignation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The proposal will be considered by the Fifa Council on 15 October. Infantino will stand for election in March 2027, with opponents facing an 18 November deadline.

gist: Richard Kenyon will lead a review of Lancashire's cricket operations and performance structure.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Incoming chief executive Richard Kenyon is set to lead a review of Lancashire's cricket operations. This follows a period where the club finished near the bottom of several competitions. The review will examine the performance environment, including staff, player contracts, and the academy pathway. This process builds upon a recent restructure that saw the departure of the director of cricket performance and the director of women's cricket.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The club aims to improve results, particularly for the men's side, following a disappointing season. Chairperson Dame Sarah Storey stated that the review is necessary to determine what changes are required to meet the club's high ambitions.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Richard Kenyon will officially take over as chief executive on 5 October. He will be guided by the club's recently published Cricket Vision to assess the necessary steps for future success.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The NFL's third week saw several close games, including the Denver Broncos beating the Los Angeles Rams 30-26. The Washington Commanders shocked the defending champion Seattle Seahawks 33-31, ending their 12-game winning streak. In Rio de Janeiro, the Baltimore Ravens defeated the Dallas Cowboys 34-31 with a late field goal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Five teams maintained their unbeaten records this season, including the surprise Las Vegas Raiders, who have already matched their entire win total from last season. Additionally, 12 of the day's 14 games were decided by eight points or fewer, tying an NFL record.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The Cleveland Browns will host divisional rivals the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles could become the sixth unbeaten team when they play the Chicago Bears on Monday.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Crystal Palace Football Club purchased an HSBC-owned site in New Beckenham, which includes a nursery and sports clubs. Childcare provider Bright Horizons informed parents by letter that the nursery faces closure in December.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Hundreds of parents signed a petition to oppose the closure. Families face finding alternative childcare at short notice, which parents warn could force reduced working hours and damage household finances.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The nursery is due to close in December. Bright Horizons stated it is committed to assisting families through the transition, while HSBC said it would offer support.

fivew: Parents, Bright Horizons, HSBC, and Crystal Palace Football Club.
